title: Streamflow Circuit-Breaker Load Harness for SSE/WSS at Scale
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a next-generation load harness that emulates realistic streaming chat/completions traffic over both Server-Sent Events (SSE) and WebSocket (WSS), with first-class support for circuit-breaker/backpressure behaviors, KV-cache affinity, tenant mixing, and automated p95 regression detection. This harness will be used by platform, runtime, and SRE teams to validate changes that affect token/sec throughput, tail latency, and stability across hosted and Dedicated deployments. It must integrate with our CI regression pipeline and emit structured telemetry consumed by console dashboards and alerting rules.
goals: Simulate mixed client populations (short-turn, long-turn, streaming-first) and realistic token emission patterns
Model connection churn and intermittent network faults while measuring p95, p99, and token/sec per-tenant
Exercise runtime circuit-breaker and backpressure policies to assert graceful degradation and fallback behavior
Be KV-cache aware: route sequences that create/benefit from KV cache and measure cache-hit effects on latency/throughput
Provide regression gating to CI: automatically compare baseline v.s. PR run and fail on configurable SLO delta
Produce artifact links (HTML reports, perf traces, flame graphs, and PR comments) and linkable run IDs
acceptance_criteria: Harness can spawn 50k concurrent logical sessions across SSE+WSS and sustain 200k tokens/sec in the synthetic peak profile
Automated p95/P99 detector that flags >10% regression against baseline and posts to PR with diffs and trace links
Circuit-breaker scenarios covered: upstream GPU OOM, shard eviction, token-generation slowdown; harness confirms fallback to lower-capacity model and logs drop/retry rates
KV-cache-aware runs show measurable latency delta when cache-hit ratio toggled; harness emits per-route cache-hit metric
CI integration proof-of-concept: a GitHub Action that runs scaled-down harness and annotates PRs with results
Run artifacts stored under perf-redwood/<run-id> and available from Console perf dashboard
design_decisions: Hybrid driver architecture: lightweight Go dispatcher for connection management + worker pool in Rust for deterministic token pacing and low-jitter stream emission
Stateful session templates: use prerecorded conversation seeds to vary prefix lengths and KV access patterns
Deterministic noise injection: configurable packet-loss, latency tail, and connection flapping to surface brittle runtime code paths
Regression comparator uses median-of-5 baseline runs to reduce noise and applies statistical significance test before gating
Use existing telemetry path (OTLP) with additional streaming-specific tags: protocol, session-type, kv-hit, model-variant, tenant-id
implementation_plan: Week 1: scaffold harness repo, implement multi-protocol connection manager, CI job skeleton
Week 2: implement token-pacing engine and session template loader; add KV-cache tagging
Week 3: add circuit-breaker scenario drivers (simulate OOM, eviction, throttling); wire telemetry metrics
Week 4: build regression comparator and PR annotator; generate reporting artifacts
Week 5: run full-scale validation on staging Dedicated cluster, tune resource caps, and document run recipes
Week 6: onboard SRE and Runtime teams, finalize runbook and alerting thresholds
risks: Running full-scale experiments on staging could affect other tenants unless isolated — requires quota and reservation tooling
False positives in regression detection due to noisy environments; needs robust baseline methodology
Harness resource footprint can be large: we must cap worker concurrency to avoid creating self-inflicted load spikes
metrics_to_capture: stream_p95 and stream_p99 latencies (end-to-end from client connect to token flush)
integration_points: Console perf dashboard (trace links + per-route breakdown)
